speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your son's condition, can you describe the consistency and frequency of his stools, and has he experienced any vomiting or bile-stained emesis?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal distension and tenderness are concerning signs. Has the baby passed any stool or gas in the last 24 hours, and does the abdomen feel firm or rigid to your touch?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the absence of fever and vomiting is notable, but we still need to rule out serious abdominal issues. I am going to order an abdominal X-ray to check for signs of obstruction or perforation, so please hold still while I review the imaging results. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an empty rectum strongly suggest a distal obstruction, which raises concern for Hirschsprung disease or meconium ileus. Has the baby passed a meconium stool within the first 48 hours of life, and has there been any history of constipation since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: The failure to pass stool normally and progressive distension strongly point toward Hirschsprung disease. I will request a contrast enema to confirm the transition zone and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Enema
